articles.title_orig: China calls for ‘fully unlocking potential’ of AI as APEC finance chiefs meet in Hong Kong
articles.title_zh: China calls for ‘fully unlocking potential’ of AI as APEC finance chiefs meet in Hong Kong
articles.content_orig:
China on Wednesday urged Asia-Pacific economies to fully harness artificial intelligence (AI) to boost productivity and economic growth as finance ministers concluded a two-day meeting in Hong Kong.
Chinese Finance Minister Lan Foan said the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting produced “practical” results, including a joint statement and a policy document on digital infrastructure financing, Hong Kong public broadcaster RTHK reported.
“We should fully unlock the potential of emerging technologies, such as AI, to raise productivity and cultivate new growth drivers,” Lan said.
He said members agreed to strengthen macroeconomic coordination, improve financial resilience and encourage private investment in digital infrastructure.
The meeting also highlighted household consumption and domestic demand as priorities for sustainable growth.
The APEC leaders’ summit is scheduled for Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, China.
The remarks come amid growing debate over AI regulation between Washington and Beijing.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently urged slowing the development of increasingly powerful AI models, warning that technological advances could outpace safety measures.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis backed aspects of his proposal.
However, US President Donald Trump rejected calls to slow development, arguing that maintaining America’s technological lead over China was essential.
Beijing has criticized proposals that could restrict China’s technological development, advocating open and inclusive international AI governance instead.

articles.title_orig: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.title_zh: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.content_orig:
United States Special Envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian leaders on the Ukraine war following “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway.
Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in the city in northwestern Russia, as the US pushes for an end to the war that began more than four and a half years ago with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Zelenskyy in recent weeks and has suggested that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf. The remarks signalled a new low in their relationship, while Zelenskyy has accused the US of suspending crucial intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as “positive”, adding that the US envoy would share the results with Putin. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also attended the talks with Zelenskyy, but did so virtually because of illness. Kushner is also expected to attend the meeting with Putin remotely.
“He’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side – and let’s see if we can make some progress,” Rubio said.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland also attended the talks in Oslo. Representatives from the European Union and NATO were present. Following Tuesday’s talks, Zelenskyy said “very, very important” intelligence from the US had been restored.
Zelenskyy has also accused Washington of slowing down the internet service, Starshield, which is crucial for Ukraine’s battlefield operations. Starshield is the military-grade equivalent of Starlink and is also developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Rubio dismissed Zelenskyy’s accusations, saying Trump had “nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield”. Musk disputes this and says such decisions can only be made by the US military and president.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk ordered the slowdown of the service, citing US officials and people familiar ⁠with the matter.
As diplomatic efforts intensify, Russia and Ukraine continue to trade long-range attacks.
At least one person was killed and two were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack in Russia’s western Bryansk ⁠region on Wednesday, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said on Telegram.
The Ukrainian Emergency Service said two people were killed in a Russian attack on a high-rise building in the Sviatoshinsky district of the capital, Kyiv.

articles.title_orig: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.title_zh: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.content_orig:
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Wednesday that trade turnover between Russia and China has increased more than 30-fold over the past 25 years despite external pressure.
Speaking at a meeting in St. Petersburg with Chinese Premier Li Qiang ahead of the 31st regular meeting between the two countries' heads of government, Mishustin added that bilateral trade was growing steadily, with nearly all transactions conducted in national currencies, the ruble and the yuan.
"Despite increased external pressure, Russia-China trade and economic cooperation has demonstrated strong momentum: over the past 25 years, our bilateral trade turnover has increased more than 30-fold," he said.
More than 90 projects across various sectors, from metallurgy to agriculture, are currently in the portfolio of the relevant bilateral commission, Mishustin said.
"Today, the share of national currencies in bilateral trade is already close to 100%," the Russian prime minister said, adding that bilateral investment was also increasing.
Mishustin called China a key economic partner, pledged continued reliable energy supplies, cited peaceful nuclear projects as a promising area, and noted that Russia remains China's top oil supplier with Power of Siberia -- the gas conduit stretching from Siberia to China -- running steadily.
"Russia will continue to reliably ensure uninterrupted energy supplies. We are also ready to strengthen cooperation in the energy sector," he said.
Bilateral agricultural trade grew by more than one-third in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, Mishustin said.
Russian products marketed under the Made in Russia brand had demonstrated their quality and were gaining popularity in China, he added.
The two countries should expand the range of goods traded between them to meet consumer demand, the Russian prime minister said.
Mutual tourist flows between Russia and China increased by approximately 50% in the first half of 2026, Mishustin said. He also called for more active modernization of border crossing points and an expansion of the geographical reach of air transport links between the countries.
Li Qiang said Russian-Chinese relations entered a new stage of more substantive and accelerated development under the strategic leadership of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
He described the regular meeting as an important opportunity to comprehensively review bilateral cooperation, address existing issues and translate agreements reached by the leaders into practical action and tangible results for their peoples.
Li said that despite changes in the international situation over recent decades, the two countries' commitment to good-neighborly relations, friendship, cooperation and development had remained unchanged.
"Adhering to the principles of non-alignment, non-confrontation and not targeting third parties, we have upheld mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation," he said, adding that Russia and China had established a model of high-level mutual trust and cooperation between major powers and neighboring countries.
The regular meeting between the Russian and Chinese heads of government is being held for the 31st time. The previous meeting took place in China in early November 2025, in Hangzhou and Beijing.

Data storage play Seagate Technology added 2% in Tuesday's regular trading, while neocloud stock CoreWeave advanced more than 1%.
This earnings season could help propel stocks as the year winds down, according to Christian Mueller-Glissmann, head of asset allocation for Goldman Sachs Research.
"Near term there might be more volatility due to [artificial intelligence] concerns, Middle East tensions and midterm elections, but we think earnings support with lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end," he wrote in a note .
Traders are also watching for results from IBM and Southwest Airlines , also due Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk confirms he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk confirms he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk has said he is actively considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, his two biggest companies.
"Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts to discuss SpaceX's latest results on Tuesday.
While Musk noted it could not be assumed a merger will go ahead, and it would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies had been formed to examine the move.
"The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there's no guarantee that they will," he said. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."
With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history.
SpaceX builds space rockets as well as Starlink internet satellites and provides a secured satellite network for governments, including the US, through its Starshield business.
That part of the business is currently facing scrutiny over claims Ukraine's access to the network has been limited, leaving it vulnerable to deadly strikes by Russia.
US President Donald Trump has denied either he or Musk ordered the slowdown . Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions.
Starlink's total revenue rose to $5.2bn in the three months to 30 September from $3bn in the same period last year. It is dwarfed by SpaceX's expansion into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, such as Anthropic and Google.
The business generated revenues of $7.5bn over the three months, up from $813m last year.
Musk, who became the world's first paper trillionaire after the SpaceX stock market debut earlier this year, said he is not included in either of the special committees considering the mega-merger.
He described himself as a "conflicted party" as the chief executive of both Tesla and SpaceX.
Even commenting on the possibility of combining the two companies, Musk compared it to "tap dancing through a minefield".
A merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, he added. At least 50% of Tesla's shareholders would need to approve a combination, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle to achieve".
Shareholders have supported Musk's desires before. Last year, a majority of investors in Tesla approved a compensation package for Musk valued at around $1tn.
While Tesla is known as an electric car company, Musk has lately been shifting resources there to work around robotics.
SpaceX, with its growing focus on AI infrastructure, quickly outstripped Tesla on the stock market in terms of value when it made its market debut in June.
SpaceX, as a whole is not profitable, despite revenue jumping to $27bn from $13.7bn over the first nine months of the year.
Over that same period it lost $1.1bn although it did report a $4.4bn profit for the most recent three months.
Following Musk's comments, SpaceX's share price rose 8% in after-hours trading. Shares in Tesla, which reports its own quarterly results on Wednesday, rose by 2%
Over the last year, Musk has taken to bringing more of his companies under fewer banners. Before it went public earlier this year, SpaceX acquired xAI and X , the platform formerly known as Twitter, both of which Musk owned.
The recent launch of Terafab, a combined effort to manufacture computer chips between Tesla and SpaceX, was another signal that Musk sees his companies as potentially more effective when working together.
Musk said on Tuesday a full merger between the two companies would make sense for the work each is doing around chips, artificial intelligence and software.

articles.title_orig: Opinion | Can China turn national power into world leadership?
articles.title_zh: Opinion | Can China turn national power into world leadership?
articles.content_orig:
China has all the signs of world-topping national strength but whether other countries accept its leadership will depend on what’s on offer
As turbulence grows in many countries, it is tempting to ask if there is a global hegemon that can sort everything out fairly.
Our latest projections of national strength for 2027 take into account resources, territory, economic strength and military power. They still put China in first place, with its lead over other countries widening. But when might China move beyond leading the ranking to exert decisive influence over the world’s trouble spots and become a global arbiter?
To explore that question, we should first look at how states have assessed national power. Ancient rulers counted people, revenues, troops, ships and resources but these were separate assessments, not a single measure of national power.

articles.title_orig: France has a proud tradition of protesting, and sometimes people lose their heads
articles.title_zh: France has a proud tradition of protesting, and sometimes people lose their heads
articles.content_orig:
France is on fire, and it faces a political and an economic reckoning that feels dangerously familiar to Americans.
The country is nearing a fiscal crisis, because it spent more than it can afford to pay back. The bill is coming due much faster than expected after bond rates surged in recent months, boosted by rising energy costs. Raising taxes and reducing government spending are part of a potential solution, but those would be politically unpopular decisions that could risk further angering an already livid public . Any workable solution faces a steep climb in an uncertain budget battle in a sharply divided government.
A growing number of countries are facing struggles similar to France’s — in particular, the United Kingdom — where rapidly growing debt, surging costs to finance that borrowing and insufficient political will to make the uncomfortable decisions to solve the problem are the story of Western economics right now. That includes the United States.
But similarities can be superficial.
France’s financial stress is particularly acute. The risk of contagion throughout Europe is low. France’s enormous public safety net represents a much larger share of government spending than that in the United States. And the unique dynamics of the American economy means the United States faces no imminent danger of becoming the next France.
These are not new problems: Europe’s social safety net has been on an unsustainable path for decades, and economists and some politicians have warned for years that the bill would eventually come due.
But they’re getting worse. The Iran war exacerbated the West’s fiscal problems.
Since February, the G7 economies’ average 10-year government bond yield grew more than 1 percentage point, reaching the highest level in nearly 20 years, the International Monetary Fund reported last week.
By the end of the decade, those seven economies’ public debt loads are expected to collectively exceed their economic production, the IMF predicts. That would be the first time since World War II.
France’s public debt is around 119% of its GDP, double the European Union’s target, and its annual budget deficit is 5.4% of its gross domestic product.
“In Europe, people are increasingly scared of the bond market and the interest rates that governments need to pay to borrow,” said Peter Taylor-Gooby, a social policy professor at the University of Kent. “It’s come to a point where you can’t ignore it anymore. If we do, we’ll reach a serious crisis.”
The rioting across France is a symptom of a much larger public and political crisis
On paper, America doesn’t look dissimilar: Its $32 trillion public debt is roughly equal to annual US GDP, and the $2 trillion budget deficit that it just closed the books on is more than 6% of GDP. The cost to finance America’s public debt just crossed $1 trillion a year , an astounding 14% of the total federal budget.
In other words, one in every seven tax dollars is used just to pay interest on the amount of money the United States is borrowing.
But the serious conversations about cutting back on spending and raising taxes taking place in Europe are considerably less serious in the United States. So why isn’t the United States facing the same problems as France?
The United States’ biggest advantage is that it prints the world’s reserve currency. The majority of global transactions are conducted in US dollars, including key commodities like oil and gold.
Demand for dollars remains robust in large part because they’re considered safe: The United States’ transparency and commitment to the rule of law make the dollar the cornerstone of the global financial system — even if some of the shine has worn off over the past decade.
That also fuels demand for US Treasuries, widely considered the safest of safe-haven assets. Even in the midst of a global government bond sell-off, US bond rates remain lower than those of other Western economies. And when stocks went on a skid last week, investors were unafraid to turn to their traditional place of refuge, sending Treasury yields sharply lower in the process.
But the difference between France and the United States really comes down to one thing. As James Carville said: It’s the economy, stupid.
The United States also has a uniquely large and diverse economy that is far less susceptible to shocks than many of its smaller peers. AI in particular is producing an investment boom in the United States that is lifting the economy when several other sectors appear to be stagnating or in decline.
One key way to make deficits less relevant is to keep the economy growing strong. That makes the debt look puny by comparison.
So countries need to ask: What is the rate we’re paying — and is it sustainable for us to keep paying it based on our expected economic growth?”
“France and the UK are pretty close,” noted Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody’s Analytics. “But in the US, AI’s contributions to growth make it more likely we’ll manage our debts and navigate it much more gracefully.”
Economists warn: Don’t confuse the lack of a looming debt crisis in the United States with fiscal responsibility. It’s just that it can handle the problem better than France or the UK.
“That doesn’t mean we should take any solace in that,” added Zandi. “We’re just in a different place.”
Any time a European country faces a fiscal problem, it raises concerns about a contagion that could spread across the continent. But economists widely view France’s problems as contained within the country.
The European Central Bank has signaled it would not need to intervene in France’s fiscal situation. But it could if it had to, and it is well-positioned to buy up a bunch of bonds of its member countries to limit any potential contagion effects, noted Andrew Kenningham, chief Europe economist at Capital Economics.
Other European economies’ deficits are also much smaller by comparison. Some are expected to run surpluses this year.
And French political parties across the left and right have said they want to remain with the European Union — including French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, a far-right candidate who once championed “Frexit” but has since backed off that pledge. Although Germany’s AfD party has advocated leaving the EU, it isn’t close to forming a government yet, Kenningham noted.
But an X factor could lead to a debt crisis outside France: the US “X date.” At some point next year, the United States will hit its debt ceiling again, and the new Congress will need to negotiate with President Donald Trump to raise it — a political football that could be particularly challenged by a lame duck president and a potentially Democratic-controlled Congress less willing to give in.
A failure to raise the debt ceiling threatens to force the United States to manufacture a default on its debt, even if it otherwise would be able to pay.
“You could construct a scenario in which we breach the debt limit by Halloween next year,” said Zandi. “And then you’ve got other issues.”

articles.title_orig: OpenAI ‘agents’ disabled their own monitoring systems
articles.title_zh: OpenAI ‘agents’ disabled their own monitoring systems
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI has revealed that agents operated by two of its most powerful models disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks, with one subsequently denying it had done so.
An agent powered by GPT Sol 6.1 disabled automatic alerts to OpenAI's security team, the company said in a blog post late on Tuesday. In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration and then falsely claimed it hadn't. The incidents happened during internal coding tasks.
"In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," OpenAI said in a blog post.
Warnings about the risks of developing increasingly advanced AI systems have ramped up in recent months, amid cyberattacks from rogue models and growing calls for a slowdown from researchers building the tech.
The latest incidents reported by OpenAI highlight how agents can autonomously weaken safety guardrails while carrying out seemingly innocuous tasks.
OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category, and the company said it was updating its misalignment monitoring system in response.

articles.title_orig: U.K. Approves Long-Stalled Jackdaw Gas Drilling Project in the North Sea
articles.title_zh: U.K. Approves Long-Stalled Jackdaw Gas Drilling Project in the North Sea
articles.content_orig:
Few believe decision will bring back city’s boom years, but workers hope it will keep as many North Sea jobs for now
UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
What does the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?
As recently as 2012, Aberdeen boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK. An ATM reportedly had the highest withdrawal rate in Europe in the 90s, as oil and gas wealth flowed through the city. House prices skyrocketed in the scramble for space as fossil fuel firms transformed the city’s grand granite houses into company offices. But that was then.
Today, “for sale” and “to let” signs punctuate the city’s main thoroughfares. Disposable income in Aberdeen has fallen by nearly 20% between 2013 and 2023 – more than any other large UK city – after a 2014 oil price shock sparked a brutal reversal in Aberdeen’s fortunes.
At the beginning of this year, demolition began on the former offices of Marathon Oil, once a base for hundreds of workers. Between 2010 and 2021, the number of people aged 20-29 fell by 16%. BP appears set to leave the city after announcing plans to divest from its North Sea business. On darker days, the spectre of former coal mining towns looms large in the minds of some residents.
“Years ago, a fund should have been set up that saved some of the oil money for Aberdeen . But that’s long gone,” said Scott, an assistant at a men’s clothing shop. “It’s a city centre like any other now. People blame the local council and the local government. I don’t know. It’s very different to how it was.”
“Twenty years ago this street was full. Now it is so quiet,” said one woman at a bus stop on Union Street.
For many Aberdonians, the government’s decision to approve the Jackdaw gasfield, located 150 miles offshore, was greeted with relief.
Critics point to the climate impact and the modest number of jobs that the new gasfield would likely support. Tessa Khan, the executive director of the anti-oil campaign group Uplift, said: “Jackdaw will provide around just 2% of our gas demand for roughly 10 years. It has been oversold and won’t stop the overall decline in North Sea jobs as it will be largely unmanned and operated remotely.”
The UN’s Environment Programme has said global carbon emission targets need to be cut by nearly a fifth in the next four years, and by close to half within a decade, to avoid overshooting climate targets by a disastrous margin.
But for oil and gas workers in the city, this is about keeping as many North Sea jobs for as long as possible, which have so far not been replaced by the renewables sector and tend to pay less.
At the heliport, offshore workers returning to dry land after a flight across stormy North Sea waters were in good spirits about the prospect of a new field.
“Jackdaw means we pay our mortgages. Without oil and gas, what am I supposed to do?” said one woman, who works offshore as a cleaner on a rig.
“Short term, the green industry isn’t going to replace this. It’s a slow process. You can’t expect it to happen overnight,” said another offshore worker.
Few think that the new gasfield will restore the city’s boomtown years. Unlike other oil cities such as Houston, Abu Dhabi and Stavanger, Aberdeen has not been able to recover from the 2014 price shock and there is growing acceptance that the decline is permanent. Many offshore oil and gas workers acknowledge that they are likely to be the last generation of their kind – and increasingly work away for weeks at a time on rigs in Africa and Asia.
More than 90% of the UK part of the North Sea basin has been exploited, compared with just over 50% in Norway, which has not outlawed new exploration licences. Jackdaw is projected to supply only 6% of the UK’s gas output at its peak. In the approval, the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, pointed to national security reasons behind her decision to back the project.
“This decision will support the country’s energy security with homegrown gas this winter and help minimise the UK’s use of imported higher emission fuels as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear.
“The decision is compatible with our legally binding climate commitments, and we remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050,” she said.
The rapidly growing renewables industry in the city has proved to be a boon for some firms: the shipping operator North Star once made all of its money from the oil and gas sector, but now nearly 80% of its operating profit comes from offshore wind. Great British Energy is headquartered in the city. Yet, the growth in the offshore wind industry has so far failed to offset the decline in oil and gas jobs in Aberdeen, and it is unclear it ever will. About 90% of offshore jobs in the northeast of Scotland remain in the oil and gas sector, supporting around 38,000 jobs compare to 4,200 in the renewables sector.
From the doldrums of the 2014 crash, Aberdeen has seen recent signs of recovery. Major regeneration works are taking place in the city centre. On a drive through the leafy west of the city, grand houses are not longer left on the market for months, said Joni Esson, a property lawyer with Simpson & Marwick.
“We’re seeing property sell for reasonable prices and a little bit of confidence coming back,” she said. “Loads of people who bought pre-2014 got in negative equity and then just couldn’t shift their homes.”
Our Union Street, a community group formed to reinvigorate the city’s main thoroughfare, has been filling empty shops after the vacancy rate reached 20%. For Bob Keiller, a former oil and gas CEO who oversees the effort, Jackdaw’s approval was a sign that the government was taking a more pragmatic approach to the fossil fuel sector – which would be a boost to the city.
“It’s symbolic. For a long time, it’s been ‘no, nothing, never, never again’. Whereas now there’s recognition that maybe it makes sense to produce your own fuel sources. It has to make economic and environmental sense, of course,” he said. “Before, it was, ‘No, not listening! Just stop oil.’ What does that mean? Everything we’ve got here just now relies on oil and gas at the moment.”

articles.title_orig: Anthropic posts $80bn loss in first half of 2026: WSJ
articles.title_zh: Anthropic posts $80bn loss in first half of 2026: WSJ
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company known for creating the chatbot Claude, recorded a net loss of more than $80bn in the first half of 2026, according to the Wall Street Journal, as the market anticipates its looming initial public offering (IPO).
The corporation also indicated it could spend up to $750bn in coming years to acquire more computing capacity, including potential deals currently under discussion, the Journal said on Tuesday.
The main driver for the loss was the $72bn in accounting charges related to changes in the value of convertible notes and other financial instruments Anthropic issued to raise funding, the report said.
The loss figure was up from $13bn a year earlier, according to a draft prospectus, a legal document corporations submit to financial regulators, for its IPO.
The figures show the hefty costs of the AI race, even as investors look more closely at whether the money companies are pouring into chips and data centres will pay off.
Anthropic also shared a list of potential risk factors, including uncertainty over how to prevent its products from doing harm, whether through sophisticated cyberattacks or blackmail by uncontrolled models.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment, and the report on the non-public information could not be immediately verified.
Reuters first reported in September that Anthropic posted a net loss of $42bn in 2025, as part of a series of exclusives from its IPO prospectus.
The company has benefited from the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps.
But some current and prospective investors who attended Anthropic’s investor day in San Francisco, California, last week are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
The investors who attended the event discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation previously expected for the November share sale.
Anthropic’s revenue jumped to $16.3bn in the six-month period that ended June 30, up from $1.1bn a year ago, while AI infrastructure spending nearly quadrupled to almost $9bn, the Journal reported.
Anthropic reported last week that AI could be months away from learning to self-replicate on everyday home devices.

articles.title_orig: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Ties as Japan, Iceland Boost Science Cooperation
articles.title_zh: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Ties as Japan, Iceland Boost Science Cooperation
articles.content_orig:
(Stock image/Russian flag, from Pixabay)
Two senior fellows from the Sasakawa Peace Foundation, Natsuhiko Otsuka and Hiroyuki Enomoto, spoke at the Arctic Circle Assembly, held in Reykjavik, Iceland, from October 8 to 10.
Speaking on October 8, Otsuka highlighted growing cooperation between China and Russia to develop Arctic shipping routes and examined the broader international implications of a new Arctic cooperation framework proposed by Moscow.
On October 10, Enomoto discussed the growing collaboration between Japanese and Icelandic scientists in Arctic research. He also emphasized the importance of "science diplomacy" as the two countries mark the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations.
Otsuka said China is "becoming a major power on the Arctic sea route," citing the rapid expansion of NewNew Shipping Line, a Chinese container shipping company established in 2022. Initially focused on shipping to Russia, the company has recently expanded its operations to include exports to Europe via the Arctic.
According to Otsuka, the company can afford the route's commercial risks because it expects "substantial cargo demand for Arctic shipping." One possible explanation is that its parent company handles shipments for both Chinese exporters and Chinese importers operating in Europe.
This gives NewNew Shipping Line an advantage, as it faces little price competition from major international shipping companies.
Japanese and South Korean shipping firms, however, face a different set of challenges. Given the geopolitical risks associated with Russia, Otsuka said it is not easy for carriers in either country to find domestic customers willing to ship goods along the Arctic route off Russia's northern coast.
On freight rates, Otsuka said the Arctic route would struggle to compete with the lower costs offered by ultra-large container ships passing through the Suez Canal.
Russia, meanwhile, faces significant challenges in developing the Arctic route. Its cargo volume targets are overly ambitious, while international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine has further complicated its plans.
Given these challenges, Otsuka said China's growing use of the route provides a much-needed boost to Russia's ambitions.
At an international conference hosted in September, Russia proposed a new framework for Arctic cooperation, seeking an alternative to the existing Arctic Council, whose seven other members continue to impose sanctions on Moscow.
Otsuka warned that the proposal could divide the region into two competing blocs: the "Arctic Seven" and a Russia-led group of sympathetic non-Arctic countries.
The Arctic Seven comprise the United States, Canada, Denmark, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Finland—all NATO members. Otsuka said the proposal could deepen tensions between NATO members in the Arctic and countries aligned with Russia.
For now, Otsuka described the prospect of establishing a new international body to rival the Arctic Council as being at an "uncertain conceptual stage."
However, he noted that growing cooperation between China and Russia on Arctic shipping is already producing tangible results. He suggested this cooperation could be a "practical step" toward establishing a new Russia-led international organization.
Speaking at a separate session, Enomoto thanked Icelandic government officials and university researchers for their contributions to growing scientific cooperation between Japan and Iceland.
Japan gained observer status on the Arctic Council in 2013 and has since strengthened its ties with Iceland through initiatives such as the Arctic Science Ministerial and the first Arctic Circle Tokyo Forum, held in 2023.
Iceland's ambassador to Japan, Hreinn Pálsson, echoed Enomoto's remarks, emphasizing the importance of science diplomacy in bilateral relations.
He also expressed hope that continued cooperation between Japanese and Icelandic scientists would help further strengthen ties between the two countries.

articles.title_orig: Garmin Edge 1060 Cycling GPS Hands-On: Everything You Need to Know!
articles.title_zh: Garmin Edge 1060 Cycling GPS Hands-On: Everything You Need to Know!
articles.content_orig:
Garmin has just announced three new cycling products in a rare mid-October cycling-focused drop. This includes the new Garmin Edge 1060 flagship cycling GPS, the Garmin Edge Explore 3/3 Plus cycling GPS, and the Tacx Nera smart trainer. But for this post, I’m going to focus on the new Edge 1060.
The new Edge 1060 got what is best described as ‘upgrades around the Edges’. It’s got a slimmed-down case, added an internal microphone for voice control and voice messaging, some new USB-C port features (and location), as well as some new routing-related features. Plus there’s a boatload of smaller enhancements, like tweaks to Strava Live Segments, the structured Workout Player, and more.
The best part is a number of these software changes are coming back to the Edge x50 series (550/850/1050), and some of them also to the Edge x40 series too. I’ll detail all of that in a post tomorrow after I finish getting everything a bit more structured.
With that, let’s simply dive right into things.
The Edge 1060 takes the core guts of the Edge 1050 (including the bright display, bike bell, speaker, battery life, etc.) and puts it in a smaller/lighter case, while adding in a microphone and a number of other software features. This does not feel like a major step forward for the Edge series, yet at the same time, it does bring the device in line with other voice features found on recent Garmin Fenix & Forerunner units.
– Added 4 physical buttons (now 7 in total, matching Edge 550/850) – Added microphone (already had full speaker) – Added voice control – Added voice messaging (via Garmin Messenger app) – Added support for Garmin Messenger app – Added Ride Readiness Checklist – Added additional route details for on-device created routes (elevation graph, expected time, etc.) – Added Free Flow Routing (routes with less slow/stop & go bits) – Added Route Preview Metrics (Closure, Hazards, Traffic, etc.) – Added Up Ahead Points of Interest (POI) both on route, and off-route – Adding Google POI transfer to Edge for Android (iPhone already has), on November 3rd – Added QWERTY keyboard – Added predictive text when typing on said keyboard – Added GroupRide feature to broadcast group ride if in group of other Edge users – Added alternate data field feature – Redesigned Workout Page to allow for collapsible portions – Redesigned Strava Live Segments page for collapsible portions – Redesigned Strava Live Segments page for competitor icons on map & elevation profile – Now allows Strava Live Segments on *any* route (not just Strava Routes) – Adding GarminLink for seamless watch heart rate broadcast (Q1 2027) – Adding Carbon Savings feature to show benefits of bike commuting (Q1 2027) – Moved USB-C charging port from back/end to underside (makes it easier to charge while riding) – Added Reserve Charging Feature – Decreased weight from 161g to 142g – Decreased case/bezel size: Now 58.5 x 107 x 16.3 mm (was 60.2 x 118.5 x 16.3 mm) – Moved speaker location for better audio to the bottom (previous charging port area) – Tweaked backlight design to have more even distribution – Same 3.5” LCD display as before – Same 480x800px display resolution (1,000nits) – Same 64GB internal storage – Same 20 hours battery life & 60 hours battery saver mode as before – Still power charging mount connector compatible – Same IPX7 waterproofing as before – Price increased from $699 to $799
I’m a little bit surprised to see the price increase there. While Garmin has increased prices on many devices over the last 2-3 years, the general Garmin trend for 2026 was actually not increasing prices. Most products stayed the same this year. I suppose it is worthwhile noting that back when the Edge 1050 came out, it actually saw a price reduction (from $749 for the previous-gen Edge 1040 Solar, down to $699 for the newer Edge 1050). So I could see some logic in that this is finally keeping up with things. I guess.
Now, for lack of anywhere else to put it below, I just want to briefly note the extra 4 buttons. This matches the Edge 550/850, which have 7 buttons, and allows you to do *anything* either via buttons or touch. This is much appreciated, and I’m glad we’re seeing the comeback in buttons across the board from numerous companies.
And here’s the end, though, these buttons got slightly smaller, but now do sit more on the edge, which should make them easier to hit with gloves and a tight-fitting Edge out-front mount.
With that, let’s dive into the new features.
(Above: Me hands-free sending a voice message that I’m going to be late to a meeting, while riding as fast/hard as I can to not be late for said meeting.)
Now, as I’ve said countless times here before on all assortments of wearables – I don’t tend to like voice-control wearables. I just don’t see the value of it most of the time. Especially for wrist-based things, where I can grab my phone far faster in almost all cases (the only real exception is something like surfing, but…I don’t surf).
Still, let’s look at what Garmin is doing here to see if it makes any sense. With that new microphone, they’ve basically added two main features:
– Added voice control – Added voice messaging (via Garmin Messenger app)
Remembering that there’s already a loudspeaker there from the Edge 1050, and that they already brought in the voice prompts (e.g., telling you to ‘Turn Left’, etc.). So this is all about you talking to your unit; your unit already was talking to you. Note that, technically speaking, the speaker remains the same, but is now moved down to the bottom of the unit where the charging port used to be. The microphone sits to the left of that.
So, starting off with when it comes to voice control, you’ll say “OK Garmin”, followed by whatever your quest (or question) is. There’s a surprising number of things it’ll respond to, albeit zero of them I can seem to remember mid-ride. Still, over time you’ll use the ones you use, and occasionally learn new ones.
At speeds up to about 50KPH, on both roadway (with rain) and gravel (with splashing water), it never missed responding to a single ‘OK Garmin’. Though whether it fully understood my question was a different matter. Most of the time, if it subsequently ignored me, it was because I phrased something differently than it expected. You’ll know whether or not it detects the ‘OK Garmin’ as it’ll have the little blue squiggly audio thing pop up at the bottom:
Now, with the voice control sorted, then we move into voice messages. This allows you to send someone a voice message purely hands-free. No touching of anything is required. You’ll say “OK Garmin, send a Voice Message to Des”, and boom, it opens up this page to send a voice message to Des. It waits about 2-3 seconds before it starts recording:
From there, you can send a 30-second voice message. At the end of which, you’ve got 10 seconds to either cancel it (manually), or simply let it fly (it’ll send automatically). Again, the goal here is being hands-free.
If, however, the speaker is triggered (e.g., a radar alert or navigation prompt), it’ll pause the recording. This can be a bit annoying in heavy traffic, making it a bit tricky to successfully finish recording a voice message. Otherwise, it worked flawlessly. The only slight downside is there isn’t a way to hands-free end a message earlier than the 30 seconds. You can certainly tap the screen, but hands-free today, you’re sending a 30-second message otherwise.
Also note that if you want to use your hands, you can assign a shifter button (like SRAM bonus buttons), or simply long-hold the lower left button to access voice control.
Once all that’s sorted, the message is sent via the Garmin Messenger app. The same Garmin Messenger as all their other devices use (e.g., inReach, Fenix, MARQ, etc.) for sending and receiving both cellular and satellite messages. This means the person on the other end must have the Garmin Messenger app. There’s no ability to tie in to either iOS or Android native messaging at this time.

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.content_orig:
This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.
The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.
PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.
Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches , and records each branch's changes in its changelog . Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers.
Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.
Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version.
PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress , with CERT-EU's isolation advice added.

Chinese scientists have developed what they say is the world’s smallest wearable mini brain monitor that can track the activity of thousands of neurons at the same time.
Weighing in at one gram (0.35 oz), the wireless “Airscope” is the lightest device of its kind and enables researchers to track a wider range of brain activity in untethered laboratory animals.

articles.content_orig:
BEIJING, Oct 21 (Reuters) - China's government said on Wednesday that its coast guard was "safeguarding order" around a tiny and strategically located Taiwan-controlled atoll at the top end of the ‌South China Sea where Taipei fears Beijing is trying to enforce jurisdiction.
China, which views democratically governed ‌Taiwan as its own territory, said last week that Taiwan must "bear the consequences" of its coast guard using a water cannon ​against a Chinese fishing boat near the Pratas Islands.
Taiwan has reported two incidents since Sunday of Chinese coast guard vessels approaching the Pratas, accusing Beijing of provocative behaviour.
Speaking at a regular news briefing, a spokesperson for China's Taiwan Affairs Office said Beijing has "indisputable sovereignty" over the South China Sea islands, including the Pratas and ‌their adjacent waters.
"Mainland coast guard vessels conducting ⁠law enforcement patrols in the relevant waters are fulfilling their duties in accordance with the law, safeguarding normal navigation and operational order," spokesperson Zhang Han told reporters.
The ⁠Chinese ships are "effectively protecting the lawful and legitimate rights and interests of people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and the safety of lives and property", she added.
The "obstinate insistence" by Taiwan's ruling party on its separatist ​stance is ​the root cause of the peril of war across ​the strait, Zhang said.
Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's ‌territorial claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.
China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan and has never renounced the use of force to bring the island under its control.
The Pratas have no permanent civilian population and lie roughly between southern Taiwan and Hong Kong. Security experts see them as vulnerable to Chinese attack due to their distance — more than 400 km (250 miles) — from Taiwan.
China's military ‌already operates around Taiwan on an almost daily basis. Taipei has ​become increasingly alarmed by Beijing's use of its coast guard to ​carry out "law enforcement" patrols to try to ​assert jurisdiction.
Addressing a forum in Taipei late Tuesday, Taiwan's top China-policy maker said Beijing ‌is attempting to "domesticate" the Taiwan issue to "create an ​illusion of having de ​facto jurisdiction over Taiwan's surrounding waters and offshore islands".
With President Xi Jinping expected to be confirmed for a fourth term in office next year, China's mission to "achieve national unification" becomes even more ​pressing, said Chiu Chui-cheng, head of ‌the Mainland Affairs Council.
"We assess that Beijing's Taiwan policy will shift toward a more aggressive, ​provocative strategy of 'exercising jurisdiction before achieving unification'," he added.

articles.title_orig: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
articles.title_zh: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
articles.content_orig:
A newly identified freshwater cave snail in China is offering scientists a rare glimpse into the little-known aquatic ecosystems hidden beneath East Asia. Published in the journal Subterranean Biology , the discovery represents an important step forward in understanding the region's underground wildlife. Until now, no freshwater cave snails had been documented in China, and the country's subterranean freshwater mollusks had received relatively little scientific attention.
The newly discovered species, Erhaia dijiang , has evolved remarkable features that allow it to live in complete darkness. As a true cave-dwelling animal, it has entirely lost its eyes, with the structures normally associated with vision having fully degenerated. The tiny snail also has a cone-shaped, nearly transparent shell, a delicate body without pigmentation, and long, slender tentacles.
Its unusual appearance inspired a name drawn from ancient Chinese mythology. Researchers chose dijiang in honor of "Di Jiang," a mountain patron god portrayed as a faceless beast in the ancient text Classic of Mountains and Seas (山海经). The connection is particularly fitting because the snail is extremely sensitive to light. During laboratory observations, individuals consistently retreated into dark spaces beneath rocks whenever they were exposed to illumination.
The location of the discovery is just as remarkable as the animal itself. Scientists found Erhaia dijiang at an elevation of 2,062 meters, making it the highest-altitude cave snail yet recorded within the family Erhaiidae. The finding demonstrates that freshwater cave snails can inhabit limestone cave systems at elevations above 2,000 meters.
Life in the Dark Waters of a Mountain Cave
Within its underground habitat, Erhaia dijiang lives among submerged gravel and broken rock in water less than one meter deep. The cave's water temperature stays close to 20°C, providing a relatively stable environment for the tiny mollusks.
Even when heavy seasonal rains increase the flow of water and occasionally wash a few snails out through the cave opening, they have not been observed in nearby streams. Researchers found that the animals remain confined to the cave environment, staying within two meters of its entrance.
Laboratory observations also provided clues about what these elusive creatures eat. The snails were seen feeding on diatoms, microscopic algae that grow on rock surfaces, and they also consumed fish food supplied by the researchers.
Only Three Living Snails Found, Raising Conservation Concerns
Although the discovery sheds new light on China's largely unexplored underground aquatic biodiversity, researchers are concerned about the species' future. They describe its conservation outlook as "far from optimistic."
During the first field investigation in August 2025, the team encountered an exceptionally small number of snails. Despite searching the shallow cave waters, researchers located only three living adults and one empty shell. They found no juveniles, suggesting that the known population is extremely sparse.
The scientists are now urging more comprehensive investigations of cave ecosystems throughout China to uncover additional species and better understand these fragile underground habitats. They also emphasize the need to develop conservation protections quickly for these vulnerable mollusks, which are native to highly restricted environments and could face serious threats before their populations are fully understood.

This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory.
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.
The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.
PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.
Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches , and records each branch's changes in its changelog . Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers.
Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.
Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version.
PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress , with CERT-EU's isolation advice added.
Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577 , a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours.

articles.title_orig: Opinion | Burnham’s Britain can learn from Trump in engaging with China
articles.title_zh: Opinion | Burnham’s Britain can learn from Trump in engaging with China
articles.content_orig:
While an IPAC report accurately notes that Britain is woefully unprepared to get relations with China right, the audit’s ideological framing is unhelpful
Getting relations with China right is widely seen as Britain’s epoch-defining challenge. It is also one it is woefully unprepared to face.
So concluded a recent audit by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), which highlighted that top negotiators lacked basic Chinese language skills. More critically, it exposed a deeper deficit: a poor grasp of China spanning political elites and the public alike. This is rooted in a desk-bound classroom sinology rather than a nuanced appreciation and lived immersion.
Yet IPAC’s audit will do little to fix this deficit. Indeed, its ideological framing will deepen it.
The report depicts China as a neo-totalitarian state seeking to engineer the souls of its citizens. It alleges that this coercive ambition extends globally, that Beijing seeks to upend the liberal world order to usher in an era favourable to authoritarian imperialism.

articles.title_orig: Man, Woman Executed for 'Indecent Acts' in Mecca Mosque
articles.title_zh: Man, Woman Executed for 'Indecent Acts' in Mecca Mosque
articles.content_orig:
Bangladeshi authorities say they were not informed of the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in the holy city of Mecca until after it had taken place, local media reports.
A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed last Wednesday after being convicted of committing an "indecent act" inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry. The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act.
Bangladesh says it has reached out to the Saudi Arabian government to ask for more details about the case.
The two Muslim countries share a close relationship due to their religious affinity and strong economic ties.
More than three million Bangladeshis work and live in Saudi Arabia, mostly in low-paying jobs, and news of the double execution has raised public concern in Bangladesh.
According to the Saudi interior ministry, the two Bangladeshi nationals were convicted and sentenced to death under "tazir", which in Islamic law refers to punishments left to the discretion of the judge.
The ministry statement said they were handed the sentences because of the severity of the offence, and the fact that they violated the "sanctity" of the mosque.
Bangladesh has reached out to the Saudi government about the offences involved and legal proceedings in the case, said state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The government would consider next steps, such as the repatriation of the bodies, after getting information from Saudi authorities, Islam said.
She added that the government was committed to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Bangladeshis abroad.
The two executed Bangladeshis were included in a list of prisoners that Saudi Arabia had shared with Bangladesh, upon a request from the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah - but that list did not indicate that the pair had been sentenced to death, the Daily Star reported.
This is not the first time that foreign nationals have been executed by Saudi authorities.
According to Amnesty International, the country has executed around 100 people this year, many of whom are foreigners convicted of drug offences.
In 2011, eight Bangladeshi men were publicly executed in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh after they were found guilty of killing an Egyptian.
Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia overturned a death sentence handed to a Sri Lankan man over a comment he had made on Facebook, which had led to him being convicted of blasphemy. That decision came after the case sparked public outcry in Sri Lanka and spurred diplomatic efforts to seek clemency for the man.

articles.title_orig: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject separation process in a victory for Carney
articles.title_zh: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject separation process in a victory for Carney
articles.content_orig:
Voters in Canada's oil-rich province of Alberta have rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence, results showed early Tuesday, delivering a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity amid President Trump's trade war and annexation threats.
The vote was not a direct referendum on independence but would have set oil-rich Alberta on a path toward a future vote on separation from Canada.
With more than 1 million votes counted, about 76% supported remaining in Canada, compared with 23% who backed beginning a process that could lead to separation.
"We are a solid country that's united from coast to coast to coast," Thomas Lukaszuk, a former Alberta deputy premier who led the Forever Canadian campaign against separation, told supporters.
Results were delayed after late openings forced more than 100 polling stations to extend voting hours Monday. More than 1.35 million Albertans, or 43% of eligible voters, cast advance or special ballots. Albertans were deciding whether to remain in Canada or begin a legal process that could have led to a second vote on separation.
Alberta, home to the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, is cowboy country and a conservative stronghold whose political culture has long had more in common with the American West than much of Canada. Resentment toward Ottawa runs deep, but has not traditionally translated into widespread support for independence.
Dustin Degenhardt, a Wainwright voter, said Albertans have long been mistreated by Ottawa.
"Alberta has essentially been treated as, you know, a colony," he said after voting Monday. "They want to take and take and take from us and not return anything."
Taylor MacIsaac, another Wainwright voter, backed separation.
"I think it'll be good for Alberta to separate personally, as a very conservative individual that grew up in rural Alberta," she said.
Dave Malka, 59, of Edmonton, criticized spending money on a "referendum on a referendum" rather than health care.
Despite the proposal's apparent failure, separatist leaders have said they turned a fringe cause into a movement that will not disappear.
Carney earlier urged Albertans to deliver a decisive vote for unity. "Vote like Canada's future depends on it because it does," he told a rally Friday in Edmonton, where he grew up.

articles.title_orig: 296 km/h: Super Typhoon Champi is now the strongest storm on Earth in 2026
articles.title_zh: 296 km/h: Super Typhoon Champi is now the strongest storm on Earth in 2026
articles.content_orig:
Super Typhoon Champi has now grown into the world’s strongest tropical cyclone of 2026, with respect to wind speed.
The system in the western Pacific Ocean became a powerhouse with its peak winds of of 296 km/h, the equivalent of a Category 5 storm.
Hurricane Polo previously held the title for world’s strongest tropical cyclone in 2026, in terms of wind speed. The storm peaked with maximum, sustained winds of 285 km/h and a minimum, central pressure of 892 mb--which is still lower than Champi's (895 mb)--making Polo stronger in that regard.
Such a low air pressure made Polo the second-most intense hurricane on record in the eastern Pacific.
Champi is also now the world’s seventh Category 5 storm of the year.
DON’T MISS: What’s the difference between hurricanes, typhoons, and cyclones?
The typhoon also had a very healthy structure on radar as it passed Guam early Sunday morning local time.
Sea surface temperatures in this section of the western Pacific are running around 30°C , which is slightly warmer than normal for this time of year. The environment around the typhoon features deep moisture, calm winds, low wind shear. and enough upper-level support to vent air away from the storm.
The massive Champi will continue to track west towards Taipei before turning northwest later this week.
It will enter a more unfavourable environment, so Champi is forecast to weaken to a Category 4 or 3 storm by Thursday and Friday.
All of those ingredients, plus the storm’s own internal organization, are critical for a tropical cyclone to maintain its composure and continue strengthening.
The massive storm is tugging on the jet stream, having an influence on weather patterns across the globe.
Champi took a more westerly track towards Taiwan. Downstream, impacts to Canada are expected , reinforcing an end-of-October and early-November pattern we have previously been forecasting.
In Ontario and Quebec, the weather is expected to become more changeable and unsettled at times during the middle of and late next week, lingering into the following week.
Warmer-than-normal temperatures are expected to dominate, but quick interruptions are also expected.

articles.title_orig: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.title_zh: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.content_orig:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.
The health minister, Muhammad Pate, said authorities had begun tracing 44 people identified as contacts of the patient. “We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” he said.
Uganda’s ministry of health said the patient had only transited through Uganda and that she is a Nigerian woman who had been on a business trip to Congo’s eastern region. The Nigerian authorities have not disclosed her nationality.
“Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said in a statement. The ministry insisted Uganda has “no confirmed active Ebola cases”.
Nigeria is the latest country to report an Ebola case as the outbreak spreads across the region. Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases, but it later declared itself free of the virus.
Dr Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centers for Disease Control, said on X that “we are facing an extremely serious threat,” with a fatality rate of nearly 50% of cases.
“This Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has already become the most geographically extensive in history, affecting several countries spread across three regions of Africa,” he said.
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control said two weeks ago it was stepping up surveillance following the detection of Ebola in Kenya and strengthening the country’s preparedness for a potential outbreak.
“These efforts have focused on early detection, isolation and referral, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, contact tracing, risk communication and protection of health care workers,” the agency said.
Nigeria established an Ebola taskforce in June after the outbreak in Congo in mid-May.
The spread of Ebola beyond Congo has heightened fears among health authorities about the rapid transmission of the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has infected more than 9,500 people and killed more than 4,600 people.
The latest Ebola outbreak is the fastest-spreading on record and is on track to exceed the deadliest on record, the 11,000 people killed in West Africa’s regional outbreak between 2014 and 2016, WHO has said.

Instead, in the run-up to the merger’s completion, Ellison added to a multibillion-dollar borrowing spree. articles.title_orig: Through Chinese eyes: a CASS scholar on Britain’s Xi Jinping Thought Study Group
articles.title_zh: Through Chinese eyes: a CASS scholar on Britain’s Xi Jinping Thought Study Group
articles.content_orig:
The following article by Zhuo Mingliang, Associate Research Fellow at the Academy of Marxism of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), examines the work of the Xi Jinping Thought Study Group, set up in 2020 by the London-based Institute for Independence Studies . Among its founders is our co-editor Keith Bennett.
Zhuo introduces the Study Group and its core members, and summarises the main arguments of its 2023 book of memoirs by long-standing friends of China. These include the view that China’s achievements demonstrate the superiority of socialism, and that Xi Jinping Thought is “a great gift to all humanity” that can help unite progressive forces worldwide. He also outlines the Institute’s distinctive positions, among them its emphasis on the non-Western development of scientific socialism and its critique of Western leftists who remain sceptical of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The article offers an interesting insight into how Chinese scholars view the work of China’s friends in the West – and into the role of people-to-people movements in breaking through the anti-China consensus in the Western media.
The article was originally published in Chinese in the Journal of Handan University (Vol. 36, No. 3, September 2026). The English translation is by Friends of Socialist China; quotations from Keith Bennett’s preface are translated back from the Chinese and will not match his original wording.
Abstract: The “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era Study Group” is an academic research organisation set up by left-wing British scholars who know China well and are friendly towards it. Writing from the standpoint of overseas people with first-hand experience, its members affirm the international influence of Xi Jinping Thought. They recognise the superiority of the socialist system as shown by China’s development path, and they rebut false anti-China narratives in the West.
Western non-governmental groups that know China and are friendly to it are an important force for breaking down US and Western media bias against China. The article therefore recommends four lines of work:
The aim is to use civil-society forces to “tell China’s story well”, grow a friendly international climate of opinion towards China, and strengthen the popular basis for people-to-people ties between China and other countries.
Keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; Britain’s Institute for Independence Studies; scientific socialism
At present, British people who know and are friendly towards China follow China’s achievements in reform and development closely. They actively study Xi Jinping Thought, Chinese modernisation, China’s global initiatives and “Chinese solutions”. In doing so they have helped improve mutual understanding between the Chinese and British peoples and helped the international community see China objectively and fairly.
One of these is the “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era Study Group”. It is an important academic body under the Institute for Independence Studies, and it works to study and spread Xi Jinping Thought in Britain and around the world. It has published a book, Paths to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: Memoirs of Long-Standing Friends of China and Solidarity Activists . Its views and positions deserve our close attention.
The Institute for Independence Studies is an independent body based in London, founded by left-wing scholars from several countries. It is dedicated to researching and spreading the ideas of social and national liberation, and to applying them to social reality in the era of imperialism. This work is carried out especially through the writings and activities of Keith Bennett.
In August 2020 the Institute set up the Study Group. Its purpose is to study and spread Xi Jinping Thought, to draw from it experience of universal significance for understanding the new era, and to promote the flourishing of intellectual, academic and cultural life in its own country. The Study Group’s first major undertaking after its founding was to edit and publish Paths to Xi Jinping Thought: Memoirs of Long-Standing Friends of China and Solidarity Activists . Published in 2023, it is a collection of memoirs by international friends and senior figures in friendship organisations who have long worked for friendship with China and firmly supported its development.
The authors draw on their own experience to review their history of engagement with China. They bear vivid witness to China’s leap forward in the new era. On that basis they explain how they understand and identify with the formation of Xi Jinping Thought and its practical power.
The book offers the distinctive observations of overseas eyewitnesses, stepping outside the usual perspectives of domestic research. It shows the far-reaching influence of Xi Jinping Thought in three areas: guiding China’s development, promoting friendship and mutual trust between China and other countries, and helping to build a community with a shared future for mankind. It also shows how this thought is being spread and recognised ever more widely in the international community.
In the book’s Preface, Keith Bennett writes:
“Today the socialist countries are the collective leading force of the international working class and progressive movement. In terms of global reach and explanatory power, Xi Jinping Thought is the most influential body of thought among these countries. British socialists, like their comrades around the world, should therefore find effective ways to guide progressive people to study and deeply understand this valuable intellectual resource. Accomplishing this task means confronting many unresolved questions. We have long felt that how to make revolution in Western Europe remains an unanswered question, and for decades since we have been searching for the answer.” [1]
Bennett regards the book as an important contribution to that search. It collects the personal experiences and reflections of some long-standing friends of China. Over several decades these people have followed varied and complex political and intellectual paths, yet each in their own way confirms that “Xi Jinping Thought has universal applicability to the great task of uniting socialists and other progressive people and arming them ideologically.” [2]
Compiling the book took hundreds of hours of collaborative work. This included in-person meetings, in-depth interviews and thematic seminars, as well as telephone and online meetings during the Covid-19 pandemic. The process produced a large body of recordings and transcripts, which give a solid basis for further research. The main pieces in the book include “China Under Xi Jinping and the Anti-Imperialist Struggle of Our Time” and “China in the Xi Jinping Era and Communism”. Its main views are as follows:
(1) China now stands at the centre of the world stage. That reality alone should be reason enough for anyone who wants to understand the world rationally to study Xi Jinping Thought in depth. For socialists everywhere the need is more urgent still, in both theory and practice: Xi Jinping Thought offers invaluable practical experience and theoretical insight for the global socialist cause.
(2) Xi Jinping Thought is the guiding thought created and summed up by the Communist Party of China and its leaders. It has led China to great transformation and great achievements. It is now fully open to the peoples of the world, a great gift to all humanity. It can unite progressive forces worldwide, arm socialists and progressives ideologically, and encourage progressive people in the West to study the theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics in depth.

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox hardware lineup is beginning to come into focus. According to a new report from Fortune , the company is gearing up to ship new hardware in the form of a handheld in 2027, followed by a full-blown console in 2028.
It's unclear if the handheld project is a first party Xbox device, or a third-party device designed and manufactured by an OEM partner like ASUS and the ROG Ally X . The console is expected to be first-party, and is likely to run a specialized version of Windows.
The report claims that Xbox and Windows have been at odds about how the OS should run on Project Helix. Windows leaders wanted the consoles to run a modified version of Windows desktop, but Xbox leaders wanted a more boutique OS experience designed for gaming.
"Tensions ran high enough that a senior Xbox executive threatened to scrap the handheld project rather than adopt the Windows build ... Xbox is now largely controlling the direction of the operating system for the project" Fortune claims.
Windows already powers the current Xbox Series consoles, as well as Xbox One. It's a modified version of the OS that the Xbox team has customized, built on top of the Windows OS core that is developed by the Windows team. It sounds like the Xbox team has decided to maintain this approach with Project Helix consoles.
Alarmingly, Fortune claims that Microsoft is currently expecting the next-gen Xbox console to cost somewhere between $1,200 and $1,800, making it the most expensive gaming console ever. It's possible that Microsoft may choose to subsidize the cost, which would bring it closer to $1,000, but nothing is confirmed.
Of course, these rumors are unconfirmed. Plans could change and schedules could slip, so nothing is set in stone until Microsoft is ready to formalize its plans officially. For now, we know that Project Helix is still in development, with first devkits expected to debut in early 2027.
